pr_title: Change (and rename) Quaternion cubic_slerp to perform component-wise cubic interpolation
pr_body:
Fixes #57951

- Function cubic_slerp changed to perform component-wise cubic interpolation and renamed to cubic_interpolate.
- Rewrote log and exp-functions based on https://users.aalto.fi/~ssarkka/pub/quat.pdf
- Added a new optional parameter to cubic_slerp that can be used to flip (or not) the quaternions to the shorter path. Default is to flip. "Base" quaternion is used as a reference (never flipped). This might be used for blending using pre-flipped (or "cached") quaternions in animation.

This breaks compatibility as cubic_slerp is renamed to cubic_interpolate.

Didn't update doc yet. I can try to do that if this pull request looks ok otherwise(?)
pr_comments: The class reference needs to be updated and @TokageItLab said this pr will be checked.

Sorry, I don't understand what's wrong as interpolation looks quite smooth here... Video from fire's fixed reproduction project ([cubic_slerp_test_duplicate_track.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/8383420/cubic_slerp_test_duplicate_track.zip)) (earlier seemed to have keys almost at the same timestamp (2.9995 and 3s))  in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57951:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50438441/180313647-20cec35b-b5fd-4f4c-b0ef-93ba03d92ff7.mp4

And from https://github.com/fire/godot-40592 :

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50438441/180315795-c8e025fa-890d-463c-8d8e-c4cd13cac472.mp4

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50438441/180318056-b9aa2ea8-e73d-42bd-af18-373272489356.mp4

This tries to take care of flipping, but only taking quaternions used in the interpolation itself into account. If I understood correctly the flipping problem is related to animation blending(?) I don't really know much about that, but isn't it a different problem? I added an optional parameter to the interpolation function to make it possible to avoid automatic flipping so it should be possible to use it in animation if so decided.

About blending though: I used kind of blending in one project where I "blended" between a quaternion (that was animated using the method in this PR) and another one formed from euler angles (because they felt more intuitive when operating in "FPS"-style coordinates with a camera). There I just used slerp to interpolate between those. But they were always quite close to one another, so maybe more generic blending causes different problems.

Exp&log-functions could indeed be leftovers. I just tried if the problems could be caused by them when kind of trying everything earlier. The document I stumbled upon approached the calculation from quite different angle and I just couldn't tell if they were identical. I can try to revert them if needed. However if this approach is "totally wrong", then it might not be necessary. ;)

> Sorry, I don't understand what's wrong as interpolation looks quite smooth here... Video from fire's fixed reproduction project ([cubic_slerp_test_duplicate_track.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/8383420/cubic_slerp_test_duplicate_track.zip)) (earlier seemed to have keys almost at the same timestamp (2.9995 and 3s)) in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57951:

Oh, that was my bad. I am very sorry. I did not realize that. I'll look into it again later in more detail.

At least from the video I can see some points that seem to be broken. Transitions like the one at 9 seconds in the second video are wrong in the cubic_interpolate, which is probably a hitch caused by a sudden sign flip.

Ah, I remembered what we had worked before on this.

This PR confused me, because it tries to interpolate quaternion values directly without using exp. That way could definitely take the shortest path, but the problem is that it is clearly not a slerp. So I remembered that you are trying to change the method name.

I and @fire were previously trying to solve this using exp map. However, we ran into a flip issue with exp map, so that issue has been left alone for now.

There are also other problems #60154 with cubic_interpolate that need to be fixed as well. So we will get back to this issue later, but if this PR-like approach is taken, it will be when we give up on the flip issue in the exp map.

> The exp/log calculation is already implemented correctly and does not need to be changed

You are right. Wrote some comparison/test code for these methods and results were identical, at least when using the quaternions used in the existing tests (which is quite a lot). Reverted the old implementations and made a commit.

> Transitions like the one at 9 seconds in the second video are wrong in the cubic_interpolate, which is probably a hitch caused by a sudden sign flip.

Investigated this a bit deeper and it was caused by quaternion dot-product between subsequent rotations being exactly 0 (every component being zero in either of the quaternions (or practically at least in this case 180 deg rotation between them around some axis)). I think I found a solution and committed a fix.

Not sure if this is related to your flipping problem with exp map (as I don't understand it well enough). But feel free to use it in your approach if you find it useful.

> This PR confused me, because it tries to interpolate quaternion values directly without using exp. That way could definitely take the shortest path, but the problem is that it is clearly not a slerp. So I remembered that you are trying to change the method name.

cubic_slerp felt quite wrong with this type of interpolation, so that's why I changed it. And you actually seemed to agree with the name change earlier if this approach to interpolation is taken (from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/57951#issuecomment-1036844786 ) ;) :

> If I cannot find a way to resolve the kickback, it may look smoother to interpolate each element directly. Then, maybe we should avoid combining slerp() and cubic_interpolation() and we should choose to interpolate each element directly as you said, and rename the method Quaternion::cubic_slerp() to Quaternion::cubic_interpolate().

> There are also other problems https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/60154 with cubic_interpolate that need to be fixed as well. So we will get back to this issue later, but if this PR-like approach is taken, it will be when we give up on the flip issue in the exp map.

I have used some kind of "arbitrary interval" cubic hermite spline interpolation, based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_Hermite_spline on my own project. I will add a comment about that into the issue mentioned.

While twiddling with this I also made some modification into the test project https://github.com/fire/godot-40592 , PR: https://github.com/fire/godot-40592/pull/3 like added a bunch of rotations with dot-product 0 into the end of the animation.

The class reference also needs to be updated.

issue_context.title: `cubic_slerp()` may take a rotation path that is not the shortest
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.dev, 3.4

### System information

Any

### Issue description

#40592 split and resend. There is a problem with the implementation of `cubic_slerp()`, it may mix non-shortest paths in the calculation.

### Steps to reproduce

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61938263/180647818-b7c9550f-462b-430a-8966-96ccde165ea6.mp4

### Minimal reproduction project

[cubic_slerp_test.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9175808/cubic_slerp_test.zip)

@GNSS-Stylist https://github.com/TokageItLab/godot/commit/5cd3792e9a6a6820343112a5d04c8500d5516ac7

There is a problem that the way to interpolate each element of the quaternion directly is spherical-interpolation, not spherical-linear-interpolation. So I tried to adapt it to exponential map, which is probably the most common solution. Can you test it?

I think it does make the behavior more consistent. However, cubic-slerp flips the current quaternion when picking the shortest path and it does not match the pre and post sign, which causes strange kickbacks sometimes. I am trying to seek a way to improve it.

Another problem is that the exponential map is an approximate expression, so it does not pass unit tests. For normal `slerp()` that is not `cubic_slerp()`, it may have to keep the old method.

---

If I cannot find a way to resolve the kickback, it may look smoother to interpolate each element directly. Then, maybe we should avoid combining `slerp()` and `cubic_interpolation()` and we should choose to interpolate each element directly as you said, and rename the method `Quaternion::cubic_slerp()` to `Quaternion::cubic_interpolate()`.

> I think it does make the behavior more consistent. However, cubic-slerp flips the current quaternion when picking the shortest path and it does not match the pre and post sign, which causes strange kickbacks sometimes. I am trying to seek a way to improve it.

Repost from #58043:

For example, if we have [*a*, *-b*, *c*, *-d*, *-e*], and the first interpolationA is [*a*, *Q*, *-b*, *c*], and the next interpolationB is [*b*, *Q*, *c*, *-d*], then, the sign of the pre value of  interpolationB will change (because there is *b* in interpolationB, but it was *-b* in interpolationA), and the interpolation-curve will be broken. 

So, even if we use exp map, cubic_slerp() requires one of the following two things for sign consistency between pre and post.

- Determine and store the sign of all keys at the start of the animation
- We need to implement the values before_to = next_pre and before_post = next_to using a special case in the track cache to pass to the next section pre and post

Linear interpolation in Basis elements has major problems, and linear interpolation in Quaternion elements still has flip problems, so implementation in the track cache may be inevitable.

Pondered this for a while... As flipped quaternion represents the same orientation with the non-flipped one, shouldn't this work in any case without a cache or such? I mean does it actually matter which quaternions are flipped as long as they are adjusted to give the shortest path between subsequent ones? My brain refuses to understand the exp map right now, though (if the issue is related to it?).

Did some quick tests by flipping (negating all components) of a some quaternions in animation and this didn't change anything, apart from some minor rounding errors causing the center box to turn green/red instead of solid green by changing z-order just enough.

Quaternions that are flipped in sign show the same orientation, but interpolation make difference the values of those quaternions.
For example, the following two interpolations with weight 0.5 should be different.
```
Quaternion(2, 1, 4, 3).blend(Quaternion(1, -2, 3, -5), 0.5) = Quaternion(1.5, -0.5, 3.5, -1)
Quaternion(2, 1, 4, 3).blend(Quaternion(-1, 2, -3, 5), 0.5) = Quaternion(0.5, 1.5, 0.5, 4)
```

The only successful way I have done in my experiments so far is to do an flip of all the key values in advance of the animation, but not during the interpolation. This ensures that the sign does not change during the interpolation process, so no odd paths are created.

I'm discussing with @fire how to implement this. For example, we could do an implicit flip every time we insert/change a Quaternion key.
